387.e: He was attended by Durdhara, Prahasta, Mahaparsva and Nikumbha who were his learned ministers. Seated comfortably and attended by the four arrogant ministers, he was puffed with pride of their strength and appeared like the entire world surrounded by four oceans.

387.sa: दुर्धरेण प्रहस्तेन महापार्श्वेन रक्षसा। मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रतत्त्वज्ञैर्निकुम्भेन च मन्त्रिणा।।5.49.11।। सुखोपविष्टं रक्षोभिश्चतुर्भिर्बलदर्पितैः। कृत्स्नं परिवृतं लोकं चतुर्भिरिव सागरैः।।5.49.12।।
387.e: He was attended by Durdhara, Prahasta, Mahaparsva and Nikumbha who were his learned ministers. Seated comfortably and attended by the four arrogant ministers, he was puffed with pride of their strength and appeared like the entire world surrounded by four oceans.

387.sa: मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रतत्त्वज्ञैरन्यैश्च शुभबुद्धिभिः। अन्वास्यमानं रक्षोभिः सुरैरिव सुरेश्वरम्।।5.49.13।।
387.e: He was attended by ogres including ministers who were intellectuals and adept in counselling. He appeared like lord Indra attended by the gods.

387.sa: अपश्यद्राक्षसपतिं हनुमानतितेजसम्। विष्ठितं मेरुशिखरे सतोयमिव तोयदम्।।5.49.14।।
387.e: Hanuman saw the highly resplendent giant king (seated on the throne) who appeared like a cloud laden with water appearing on the peak of mount Meru.

387.sa: स तैस्सम्पीड्यमानोऽपि रक्षोभिर्भीमविक्रमैः। विस्मयं परमं गत्वा रक्षोधिपमवैक्षत।।5.49.15।।
387.e: Hanuman looked at the demon king with great amazement even while he was dealt harshly by the demons of fierce valour.

387.sa: भ्राजमानं ततो दृष्ट्वा हनुमान्राक्षसेश्वरम्। मनसा चिन्तयामास तेजसा तस्य मोहितः।।5.49.16।।
387.e: Seeing the splendour of the lord of demons, Hanuman was dimayed and started thinking thus:

387.sa: अहो रूपमहो धैर्यमहो सत्त्वमहो द्युतिः। अहो राक्षसराजस्य सर्वलक्षणयुक्तता।।5.49.17।।
387.e: 'Oh what charm what courage what strength what splendour How great is this demonking, an endowment of all merits.

387.sa: यद्यधर्मो न बलवान् स्यादयं राक्षसेश्वरः। स्यादयं सुरलोकस्य सशक्रस्यापि रक्षिता।।5.49.18।।
387.e: 'If only this lord of demons was not unrighteous, he could have become even the lord (protector) of gods including Indra.

387.sa: अस्य क्रूरैर्नृशंसैश्च कर्मभिर्लोककुत्सितैः। सर्वे बिभ्यति खल्वस्माल्लोकास्सामरदानवाः।।5.49.19।। अयं ह्युत्सहते क्रुद्धः कर्तुमेकार्णवं जगत्।
387.e: 'This Ravana has done many cruel, fierce and contemptible deeds. That is why even the demons, gods and all the people of this world get scared of him. He will render the entire world into a single ocean when he turns angry'.

387.sa: इति चिन्तां बहुविधामकरोन्मतिमान् हरिः।।5.49.20।। दृष्ट्वा राक्षसराजस्य प्रभावममितौजसः।
387.e: Many such thoughts crossed Hanuman's intelligent mind on seeing Ravana's brilliance and power. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyninth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

388.sa: तमुद्वीक्ष्य महाबाहुः पिङ्गाक्षं पुरत स्थितम्। कोपेन महताऽविष्टो रावणो लोकरावणः।।5.50.1।। शङ्काहृतात्मा दध्यौ स कपीन्द्रं तेजसावृतम्।
388.e: The mighty armed Ravana, a tormentor of all worlds, overcome with anger beheld the tawnyeyed brilliant lord of monkeys who stood before him and started thinking in his mind full of apprehensions.

388.sa: किमेष भगवान्नन्दी भवेत्साक्षादिहागतः।।5.50.2।। येन शप्तोऽस्मि कैलासे मया सञ्चालिते पुरा। सोऽयं वानरमूर्तिस्स्यात्किंस्विद्बाणो महाऽसुरः।।5.50.3।।
388.e: 'Is he Lord Nandi who came here in person? I was earlier cursed by him when I shook the mount Kailasa in the past. Could he have assumed a monkeyform or may be he is the great demon Bana. (Nandi is the bull, the vehicle of Lord Siva).

388.sa: किमेष भगवान्नन्दी भवेत्साक्षादिहागतः।।5.50.2।। येन शप्तोऽस्मि कैलासे मया सञ्चालिते पुरा। सोऽयं वानरमूर्तिस्स्यात्किंस्विद्बाणो महाऽसुरः।।5.50.3।।
388.e: 'Is he Lord Nandi who came here in person? I was earlier cursed by him when I shook the mount Kailasa in the past. Could he have assumed a monkeyform or may be he is the great demon Bana. (Nandi is the bull, the vehicle of Lord Siva).

388.sa: स राजा रोषताम्राक्षः प्रहस्तं मन्त्रिसत्तमम्। कालयुक्तमुवाचेदं वचोऽविपुलमर्थवत्।।5.50.4।।
388.e: The infuriated demon king told the great minister Prahasta, these  profound words in a brief manner appropriate to the hour.

388.sa: दुरात्मा पृच्छ्यतामेष कुतः किं वात्र कारणम्। वनभङ्गे च कोऽस्यार्थो राक्षसीनां च तर्जने।।5.50.5।।
388.e: "Enquire from this wicked one, why he has come and from where, Why he destroyed the garden and for what purpose he threatened the demonesses?

388.sa: मत्पुरीमप्रधृष्यां वाऽगमने किं प्रयोजनम्। आयोधने वा किं कार्यं पृच्छयतामेष दुर्मतिः।।5.50.6।।
388.e: "Enquire why this wicked one entered this inviolable city and for what purpose did he wage a war"

388.sa: रावणस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा प्रहस्तो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते न भीः कार्या त्वया कपे।।5.50.7।।
388.e: On hearing Ravana, Prahasta spoke these words boosting the monkey's morale 'O monkey Be relaxed. Feel safe. You need not entertain any fear.

388.sa: यदि तावत्त्वमिन्द्रेण प्रेषितो रावणालयम्। तत्त्वमाख्याहि मा भूत्ते भयं वानर मोक्ष्यसे।।5.50.8।।
388.e: "Have you came to the abode of Ravana sent by Indra? Speak the truth. Be not afraid.You will be released".

388.sa: यदि वैश्रवणस्य त्वं यमस्य वरुणस्य च। चाररूपमिदं कृत्वा प्रविष्टो नः पुरीमिमाम्।।5.50.9।। विष्णुना प्रेषितो वाऽपि दूतो विजयकाङ्क्षिणा।
न हि ते वानरं तेजो रूपमात्रं तु वानरम्।।5.50.10।। तत्त्वत: कथयस्वाद्य ततो वानर मोक्ष्यसे।
388.e: "Your appearance is only of that of a vanara. But your glow is not of a vanara indeed. Tell the truth today. You will be set free.

388.sa: अनृतं वदतश्चापि दुर्लभं तव जीवितम्।।5.50.11।। अथवा यन्निमित्तस्ते प्रवेशो रावणालये।
388.e: "If you tell a lie, it will be difficult for you to live. Or else, tell me for what reason have you entered the abode of Ravana.'

388.sa: एवमुक्तो हरिश्रेष्ठस्तदा रक्षोगणेश्वरम्।।5.50.12।। अब्रवीन्नास्मि शक्रस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य वा। धनदेन न मे सख्यं विष्णुना नास्मि चोदितः।।5.50.13।। जातिरेव मम त्वेषा वानरोऽहमिहागतः।
388.e: The foremost of the vanaras spoke to the lord of ogres in response to the equiries made to him: "I have not come from Indra or Yama or Varuna. I have no friendship with Kubera. I have not been sent by Visnu. By birth I am vanara and I have come here.'

388.sa: एवमुक्तो हरिश्रेष्ठस्तदा रक्षोगणेश्वरम्।।5.50.12।। अब्रवीन्नास्मि शक्रस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य वा। धनदेन न मे सख्यं विष्णुना नास्मि चोदितः।।5.50.13।। जातिरेव मम त्वेषा वानरोऽहमिहागतः।
388.e: The foremost of the vanaras spoke to the lord of ogres in response to the equiries made to him: "I have not come from Indra or Yama or Varuna. I have no friendship with Kubera. I have not been sent by Visnu. By birth I am vanara and I have come here.'

388.sa: दर्शने राक्षसेन्द्रस्य दुर्लभे तदिदं मया।।5.50.14।। वनं राक्षसराजस्य दर्शनार्थे विनाशितम्।
ततस्ते राक्षसाः प्राप्ता बलिनो युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः। रक्षणार्थं तु देहस्य प्रतियुद्धा मया रणे।।5.50.15।।
388.e: "Desiring to fight with me the powerful ogres came. Then I fought in self defence.

388.sa: अस्त्रपाशैर्न शक्योऽहं बद्धुं देवासुरैरपि।।5.50.16।। पितामहादेष वरो मामाप्येषोऽभ्युपागतः।
388.e: "It is not possible to bind me with any bondage of astras even by devas or danavas. Such a boon has been granted to me by Grandfather Brahma.

388.sa: राजानं द्रष्टुकामेन मयास्त्रमनुवर्तितम्।।5.50.17।। विमुक्तो ह्यहमस्त्रेण राक्षसैस्त्वभिपीडितः। केनचिद्राजकार्येण सम्प्राप्तोऽस्मि तवान्तिकम्।।5.50.18।।
388.e: "Wishing to see the king I honoured this astra and not otherwise. Even though I was tormented by the ogres and released by the astra I submitted to you as I have a small work assigned by the king.

388.sa: राजानं द्रष्टुकामेन मयास्त्रमनुवर्तितम्।।5.50.17।। विमुक्तो ह्यहमस्त्रेण राक्षसैस्त्वभिपीडितः। केनचिद्राजकार्येण सम्प्राप्तोऽस्मि तवान्तिकम्।।5.50.18।।
388.e: "Wishing to see the king I honoured this astra and not otherwise. Even though I was tormented by the ogres and released by the astra I submitted to you as I have a small work assigned by the king.

388.sa: दूतोऽहमिति विज्ञेयो राघवस्यामितौजसः। श्रूयतां चापि वचनं मम पथ्यमिदं प्रभो।।5.50.19।।
388.e: Know that I am a messenger of the highly powerful Rama. O lord please listen to these beneficial words of mine meant for your welfare. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftieth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

389.sa: तं समीक्ष्य महासत्त्वं सत्त्ववान्हरिसत्तमः। वाक्यमर्थवदव्यग्रस्तमुवाच दशाननम्।।5.51.1।।
389.e: Hanuman, the best of monkeys, looking at the very powerful Ravana spoke slowly  these highly meaningful words.

389.sa: अहं सुग्रीवसंदेशादिह प्राप्तस्तवालयम्। राक्षसेन्द्र हरीशस्त्वां भ्राता कुशलमब्रवीत्।।5.51.2।।
389.e: "O lord of demons I reached your realm here by the orders of Sugriva, lord of monkeys who is like your brother. He conveys his good wishes to you.

389.sa: भ्रातुश्शृणु समादेशं सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। धर्मार्थोपहितं वाक्यमिह चामुत्र च क्षमम्।।5.51.3।।
389.e: "The great Sugriva who is like your brother sends you a message pertinent to this world and the other world, that which is beneficial and consistent with righteousness and propriety (धर्म and अर्थ). Listen:

389.sa: राजा दशरथो नाम रथकुञ्जरवाजिमान्। पितेव बन्धुर्लोकस्य सुरेश्वरसमद्युतिः।।5.51.4।।
389.e: "There was an emperor named Dasaratha richly endowed with chariots, horses and elephants. He was a friend to the world and was like a father and equal to Indra in splendour.

389.sa: ज्येष्ठस्तस्य महाबाहुः पुत्रः प्रियकरः प्रभुः। पितुर्निदेशान्निष्क्रान्तः प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्।।5.51.5।। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया चापि भार्यया। रामो नाम महातेजा धर्म्यं पन्थानमास्थितः।।5.51.6।।
389.e: "His eldest son, a highly effulgent one, named Rama who was dear to the king, accepting his father's orders went into exile with brother Lakshmana and wife Sita also accepting a righteous path and entered Dandaka forest.

389.sa: ज्येष्ठस्तस्य महाबाहुः पुत्रः प्रियकरः प्रभुः। पितुर्निदेशान्निष्क्रान्तः प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्।।5.51.5।। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया चापि भार्यया। रामो नाम महातेजा धर्म्यं पन्थानमास्थितः।।5.51.6।।
389.e: "His eldest son, a highly effulgent one, named Rama who was dear to the king, accepting his father's orders went into exile with brother Lakshmana and wife Sita also accepting a righteous path and entered Dandaka forest.

389.sa: तस्य भार्या वने नष्टा सीता पतिमनुव्रता। वैदेहस्य सुता राज्ञो जनकस्य महात्मनः।।5.51.7।।
389.e: "Sita, daughter of king Janaka of Videha kingdom, loyally followed her husband, Rama. She was lost in the forest.

389.sa: स मार्गमाणस्तां देवीं राजपुत्रः सहानुजः। ऋश्यमूकमनुप्राप्त: सुग्रीवेण समागतः।।5.51.8।।
389.e: "Searching for the divine lady the prince reached mount Rshyamuka along with his brother and there he met Sugriva.

389.sa: तस्य तेन प्रतिज्ञातं सीतायाः परिमार्गणम्। सुग्रीवस्यापि रामेण हरिराज्यं निवेदितम्।।5.51.9।।
389.e: "Sugriva promised Rama to undertake search for Sita and Rama assured Sugriva of securing him the kingdom of the monkeys.

389.sa: ततस्तेन मृधे हत्वा राजपुत्रेण वालिनम्। सुग्रीवः स्थापितो राज्ये हर्यृक्षाणां गणेश्वरः।।5.51.10।।
389.e: "Then prince Rama killed Vali in battle and made Sugriva, king of the vanaras and bears and restored the kingship of Sugriva.

389.sa: त्वया विज्ञातपूर्वश्च वाली वानरपुङ्गवः। रामेण निहतस्सङ्ख्ये शरेणैकेन वानरः।।5.51.11।।
389.e: "You know of Vali, chief of the vanaras, in the past. Rama killed him with a single arrow in the combat.

389.sa: स सीतामार्गणे व्यग्रस्सुग्रीवः सत्यसङ्गरः। हरीन् सम्प्रेषयामास दिशस्सर्वा हरीश्वरः।।5.51.12।।
389.e: "Sugriva, who is true to his word and a faithful warrior, king of monkeys anxiously sent vanaras in all directions for searching Sita.

389.sa: तां हरीणां सहस्राणि शतानि नियुतानि च। दिक्षु सर्वासु मार्गन्ते ह्यधश्चोपरि चाम्बरे।।5.51.13।।
389.e: "Hundreds, thousands and unlimited number of monkeys are searching (for Sita) in all directions, in the underworld and heavens and the sky.

389.sa: वैनतेयसमाः केचित्केचित्तत्रानिलोपमाः। असङ्गगतयशशीघ्रा हरिवीरा महाबलाः।।5.51.14।।
389.e: "Some of the very powerful heroes equal to Garuda, equal to the Windgod (in swiftness) have gone (in quest of Sita) without touching the earth.

389.sa: अहं तु हनुमान्नाम मारुतस्यौरसस्सुतः। सीतायास्तु कृते तूर्णं शतयोजनमायतम्।।5.51.15।। समुद्रं लङ्घयित्वैव तां दिदृक्षुरिहागतः।
389.e: "I, Maruta's son, Hanuman by name too came swiftly leaping across a hundred yojanas across the ocean searching for Sita.

389.sa: भ्रमता च मया दृष्टा गृहे ते जनकात्मजा।।5.51.16।। तद्भवान् दृष्टधर्मार्थस्तपःकृतपरिग्रहः। परदारान् महाप्राज्ञ नोपरोद्धुं त्वमर्हसि।।5.51.17।।
389.e: "While I was roaming I saw Janaka's daughter Sita at your house.You are a knower of the truth of righteousness. You are very wise and carrried out great austerities. It does not behove you to abduct another man's wife.

389.sa: भ्रमता च मया दृष्टा गृहे ते जनकात्मजा।।5.51.16।। तद्भवान् दृष्टधर्मार्थस्तपःकृतपरिग्रहः। परदारान् महाप्राज्ञ नोपरोद्धुं त्वमर्हसि।।5.51.17।।
389.e: "While I was roaming I saw Janaka's daughter Sita at your house.You are a knower of the truth of righteousness. You are very wise and carrried out great austerities. It does not behove you to abduct another man's wife.

389.sa: न हि धर्मविरुद्धेषु बह्वपायेषु कर्मसु। मूलघातिषु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः।।5.51.18।।
389.e: "Indeed, respectable people and wise men like you should not indulge in actions opposed to righteousness as it will strike at the very root of your existence.

389.sa: कश्च लक्ष्मणमुक्तानां रामकोपानुवर्तिनाम्। शराणामग्रतः स्थातुं शक्तो देवासुरेष्वपि।।5.51.19।।
389.e: "Who, even among gods and asuras can withstand the arrows released by Lakshmana in obedience to the infuriated Rama's orders?

389.sa: न चापि त्रिषु लोकेषु राजन्विद्येत कश्चन। राघवस्य व्यलीकं यः कृत्वा सुखमवाप्नुयात्।।5.51.20।।
389.e: "O king  there is none in these three worlds who can enjoy happiness by displeasing Rama.

389.sa: तत् त्रिकालहितं वाक्यं धर्म्यमर्थानुबन्धि च। मन्यस्व नरदेवाय जानकी प्रतिदीयताम्।।5.51.21।।
389.e: "Think that my advice is beneficial to you for you present, past and future. It is righteous. It will provide you material wealth too. Hence return Sita to the lord of the people.

389.sa: दृष्टा हीयं मया देवी लब्धं यदिह दुर्लभम्। उत्तरं कर्म यच्छेषं निमित्तं तत्र राघवः।।5.51.22।।
389.e: "I have actually spotted the divine lady here which was most difficult. Rama will plan the remaining course of action.

389.sa: लक्षितेयं मया सीता तथा शोकपरायणा। गृह्य यां नाभिजानासि पञ्चास्यामिव पन्नगीम्।।5.51.23।।
389.e: "I have seen Sita immersed in deep sorrow. You do not realise that by abducting her you are keeping a fivehooded female serpent in your house.

389.sa: नेयं जरयितुं शक्या सासुरैरमरैरपि। विषसंसृष्टमत्यर्थं भुक्तमन्नमिवौजसा ।।5.51.24।।
389.e: "Just as food mixed with venom cannot be digested by the great fire (fire of hunger), it is not possible to keep Sita even by gods and demons. (Sita is like food mixed with poison. Ravana cannot digest her with all his power.)

389.sa: तपस्सन्तापलब्धस्ते योऽयं धर्मपरिग्रहः। न स नाशयितुं न्याय्य आत्मप्राणपरिग्रहः।।5.51.25।।
389.e: "You have acquired the merit of righteousness by prolonged hardships experienced during your penance. It is not proper to forfeit your own life in this way.

389.sa: अवध्यतां तपोभिर्यां भवान् समनुपश्यति। आत्मनः सासुरैर्देवैर्हेतुस्तत्राप्ययं महान्।।5.51.26।।
389.e: "You know you will not be killed by asuras or gods. In that case also this (keeping Sita with you) may be the prime cause of your death.

389.sa: सुग्रीवो न हि देवोऽयं नासुरो न च राक्षसः। न दानवो न गन्धर्वो न यक्षो न च पन्नगः।।5.51.27।। तस्मात्प्राणपरित्राणं कथं राजन्करिष्यसि।
389.e: "Sugriva is not an demon, nor a danava nor gandharva, nor a yaksha nor even a pannaga. Therefore how can you save your life from Sugriva?

389.sa: न तु धर्मोपसंहारमधर्मफलसंहितम्।।5.51.28।। तदेव फलमन्वेति धर्मश्चाधर्मनाशन:।
389.e: "The fruit of dharma does not accrue to one who has reached the culmination of  adharma. Unrighteousness will destroy  the fruits of righteousness.

389.sa: प्राप्तं धर्मफलं तावद्भवता नात्र संशयः। फलमस्याप्यधर्मस्य क्षिप्रमेव प्रपत्स्यसे।।5.51.29।।
389.e: "There is no doubt you have earned merit through righteousness (dharma destroys adharma and yields sweet fruit ultimately). But now you will quickly reap the result of your unrighteousness also.

389.sa: जनस्थानवधं बुद्ध्वा बुद्ध्वा वालिवधं तथा।।5.51.30।। रामसुग्रीवसख्यं च बुध्यस्व हितमात्मनः।
389.e: "You know about the killing of all ogres at Janasthana and of Vali also. You know about the alliance of Rama and Sugriva. You may  decide on a proper course of action for the sake of your own welfare.

389.sa: कामं खल्वहमप्येकस्सवाजिरथकुञ्जराम्।।5.51.31।। लङ्कां नाशयितुं शक्तस्तस्यैष तु न निश्चयः।
389.e: " Alone, I can destroy this entire Lanka teeming with horses, chariots and elephants. Indeed I have the energy but not the mandate of Sri Rama.

389.sa: रामेण हि प्रतिज्ञातं हर्यृक्षगणसन्निधौ।।5.51.32।। उत्सादनममित्राणां सीता यैस्तु प्रधर्षिता।
389.e: "Rama made a vow in the presence of bears and vanaras that he would exterminate the arrogant enemy troops  by whom Sita is abducted and assaulted.

389.sa: अपकुर्वन् हि रामस्य साक्षादपि पुरन्दरः।।5.51.33।। न सुखं प्राप्नुयादन्यः किं पुनस्त्वद्विधो जनः।
389.e: "Indra, the destroyer of enemy citadels cannot live happily if he offends Rama. What to speak of persons like you?

389.sa: यां सीतेत्यभिजानासि येयं तिष्ठति ते वशे।।5.51.34।। कालरात्रीति तां विद्धि सर्वलङ्काविनाशिनीम्।
389.e: "Sita who is under your custody is no ordinary lady. She is indeed the dark night of dissolution, destroyer of entire Lanka. Know this.

389.sa: तदलं कालपाशेन सीताविग्रहरूपिणा।।5.51.35।। स्वयं स्कन्धावसक्तेन क्षेममात्मनि चिन्त्यताम्।
389.e: "Stop holding the noose of death in Sita's form whom you yourself have placed on your shoulders. Think of your own welfare.

389.sa: सीतायास्तेजसा दग्धां रामकोपप्रपीडिताम्।।5.51.36।। दह्यमानामिमां पश्य पुरीं साट्टप्रतोलिकाम्।
389.e: "Visualize this city of Lanka including its marketplaces and main streets as  burnt by Sita's power of chastity and  Rama's anger.

389.sa: स्वानि मित्राणि मन्त्रींश्च ज्ञातीन् भ्रात्रून् सुतान् हितान्।।5.51.37।। भोगान्दारांश्च लङ्कां च मा विनाशमुपानय।
389.e: "Do not pave the path of your friends, ministers, clan, brothers and sisters, sons, wellwishers, wives and luxuries and Lanka to destruction.

389.sa: सत्यं राक्षसराजेन्द्र शृणुष्व वचनं मम।।5.51.38।। रामदासस्य दूतस्य वानरस्य विशेषतः।
389.e: "O king of demon listen to the words of truth of the servant of Rama, his messenger and specially a vanara.

389.sa: सर्वान् लोकान् सुसंहृत्य सभूतान् सचराचरान्।।5.51.39।। पुनरेव तथा स्रष्टुं शक्तो रामो महायशाः।
389.e: "Illustrious Rama can put an end  to and dissolve all creatures including both movable and immovables of all worlds. He can recreate all of them in the same way. He has such superhuman powers.

389.sa: देवासुरनरेन्द्रेषु यक्षरक्षोगणेषु च।।5.51.40।। विद्याधरेषु सर्वेषु गन्धर्वेषूरगेषु च। सिद्धेषु किन्नरेन्द्रेषु पतत्रिषु च सर्वतः।।5.51.41।। सर्वभूतेषु सर्वत्र सर्वकालेषु नास्ति सः। यो रामं प्रतियुध्येत विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमम्।।5.51.42।।
389.e: "He is equal to Visnu in valour. There is none who can dare face his rage, be it among gods, asuras, yakshas, rakshasas, vidyadharas, gandharvas uragas, siddhas, kings of kinnaras, birds and all beings at all places and at all times.

389.sa: देवासुरनरेन्द्रेषु यक्षरक्षोगणेषु च।।5.51.40।। विद्याधरेषु सर्वेषु गन्धर्वेषूरगेषु च। सिद्धेषु किन्नरेन्द्रेषु पतत्रिषु च सर्वतः।।5.51.41।। सर्वभूतेषु सर्वत्र सर्वकालेषु नास्ति सः। यो रामं प्रतियुध्येत विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमम्।।5.51.42।।
389.e: "He is equal to Visnu in valour. There is none who can dare face his rage, be it among gods, asuras, yakshas, rakshasas, vidyadharas, gandharvas uragas, siddhas, kings of kinnaras, birds and all beings at all places and at all times.

389.sa: देवासुरनरेन्द्रेषु यक्षरक्षोगणेषु च।।5.51.40।। विद्याधरेषु सर्वेषु गन्धर्वेषूरगेषु च। सिद्धेषु किन्नरेन्द्रेषु पतत्रिषु च सर्वतः।।5.51.41।। सर्वभूतेषु सर्वत्र सर्वकालेषु नास्ति सः। यो रामं प्रतियुध्येत विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमम्।।5.51.42।।
389.e: "He is equal to Visnu in valour. There is none who can dare face his rage, be it among gods, asuras, yakshas, rakshasas, vidyadharas, gandharvas uragas, siddhas, kings of kinnaras, birds and all beings at all places and at all times.

389.sa: सर्वलोकेश्वरस्यैवं कृत्वा विप्रियमुत्तमम्। रामस्य राजसिंहस्य दुर्लभं तव जीवितम्।।5.51.43।।
389.e: "Rama is the supreme lord of all worlds, a lion among kings. Having pained him it is very difficult for you to sustain your life after offending him to this extent.

389.sa: देवाश्च दैत्याश्च निशाचरेन्द्र गन्धर्वविद्याधरनागयक्षाः। रामस्य लोकत्रयनायकस्य स्थातुं न शक्तास्समरेषु सर्वे।।5.51.44।।
389.e: "O king of demons, even devas, daityas, gandharvas, vidyadharas, nagas, and yakshas are incompetent to face Rama the lord of the three worlds in wars.

389.sa: ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूश्चतुराननो वा रुद्रस्त्रिणेत्रस्त्रिपुरान्तको वा। इन्द्रो महेन्द्रस्सुरनायको वा त्रातुं न शक्ता युधि रामवध्यम्।।5.51.45।।
389.e: "Even the selfborn, fourfaced Brahma, the threeeyed Siva who destroyed Tripura, Mahendra, the king of suras do not have the power to save one whom Rama decides to kill".

389.sa: स सौष्ठवोपेतमदीनवादिनः कपेर्निशम्याप्रतिमोऽप्रियं वचः। दशाननः कोपविवृत्तलोचनः समादिशत्तस्य वधं महाकपेः।।5.51.46।।
389.e: The tenheaded Ravana who was of matchless strength, hearing the unpleasant words of advice and warning expressed skilfully with dignity by the great Hanuman, enraged Ravana, his eyes rolling in anger ordered the execution of Hanuman. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfirst sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

390.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वानरस्य महात्मनः। आज्ञापयद्वधं तस्य रावणः क्रोधमूर्छितः।।5.52.1।।
390.e: Hearing the great vanara's speech, Ravana overwhelmed with anger ordered the execution of Hanuman.

390.sa: वधे तस्य समाज्ञप्ते रावणेन दुरात्मना। निवेदितवतो दौत्यं नानुमेने विभीषणः।।5.52.2।।
390.e: Vibhishana did not approve of the killing of Hanuman, who had declared that he was an envoy (of Sri Rama) when the wicked Ravana ordered his murder.

390.sa: तं रक्षोधिपतिं क्रुद्धं तच्च कार्यमुपस्थितम्। विदित्वा चिन्तयामास कार्यं कार्यविधौ स्थितः।।5.52.3।।
390.e: Vibhishana who stood by the right course of action, having realised that the lord of demons was angry pondered over his duty.

390.sa: निश्चितार्थस्ततस्साम्ना पूज्यं शत्रुजिदग्रजम्। उवाच हितमत्यर्थं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः।।5.52.4।।
390.e: Then Vibhishana, who was skilled in speech having decided about his duty   addressed his reverential elder brother, a conqueror of enemies in soothing, words in a meaningful, wholesome manner.

390.sa: क्षमस्व रोषं त्यज राक्षसेन्द्र प्रसीद मद्वाक्यमिदं शृणुष्व। वधं न कुर्वन्ति परावरज्ञा दूतस्य सन्तो वसुधाधिपेन्द्राः।।5.52.5।।
390.e: "O king of ogres give up your wrath, forgive and calm down. Please listen to my appeal. You know the basic values of life. Virtuous rulers of the earth do not order killing of an envoy.

390.sa: राजधर्मविरुद्धं च लोकवृत्तेश्च गर्हितम्। तव चासदृशं वीर कपेरस्य प्रमापणम्।।5.52.6।।
390.e: "Mighty king killing this Hanuman is contrary to righteousness of kings. This is deplorable diplomacy and also unbecoming of you.

390.sa: धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च राजधर्मविशारदः। परावरज्ञो भूतानां त्वमेव परमार्थवित्।।5.52.7।।
390.e: "You are conversant with  dharma of a king.  You have a sense of gratitude. You are a knower of right and wrong of all beings. the supeme truth.

390.sa: गृह्यन्ते यदि रोषेण त्वादृशोऽपि विचक्षणः। तत श्शास्त्रविपश्चित्त्वं श्रम एव हि केवलम्।।5.52.8।।
390.e: "If wise persons like you are also overpowered by unjust anger, then the mastery of  the scriptures will become a mere fruitless exercise.

390.sa: तस्मात्प्रसीद शत्रुघ्न राक्षसेन्द्र दुरासद। युक्तायुक्तं विनिश्चित्य दूतदण्डो विधीयताम्।।5.52.9।।
390.e: "O destroyer of foes, O unassailable king of demon calm down. Only after carefully considering what is proper and improper decide on the punishment to be imposed".

390.sa: विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। रोषेण महताविष्टो वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्।।5.52.10।।
390.e: Ravana, the lord of demons heard Vibhishana's words and overcome with anger replied:

390.sa: न पापानां वधे पापं विद्यते शत्रुसूदन। तस्मादेनं वधिष्यामि वानरं पापचारिणम्।।5.52.11।।
390.e: "O slayer of foes it is not wrong to kill a sinner. I shall, therefore, kill the sinful vanara."

390.sa: अधर्ममूलं बहुदोषयुक्तमनार्यजुष्टं वचनं निशम्य। उवाच वाक्यं परमार्थतत्त्वं विभीषणो बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठः।।5.52.12।।
390.e: On hearing his brother's harsh words spoken in tremendous anger, which were not acceptable to noble souls, wise Vibhishana again spoke these words of supreme truth:

390.sa: प्रसीद लङ्केश्वर राक्षसेन्द्र धर्मार्थयुक्तं वचनं शृणुष्व। दूतानवध्यान् समयेषु राजन् सर्वेषु सर्वत्र वदन्ति सन्तः।।5.52.13।।
390.e: "O lord of Lanka O king of demons be pleased to listen to my words which are the essence of dharma and artha. The elders have declared that the emissaries should not be killed by any means.

390.sa: असंशयं शत्रुरयं प्रवृद्धः कृतं ह्यनेनाप्रियमप्रमेयम्। न दूतवध्यां प्रवदन्ति सन्तो दूतस्य दृष्टा बहवो हि दण्डाः।।5.52.14।।
390.e: This enemy has done a lot of harm, no doubt. Indeed he has done terrible and unpleasant deeds. (Yet) the wise have recommended many alternate punishments, while prohibiting their killing.

390.sa: वैरूप्यमङ्गेषु कशाभिघातो मौण्ड्यं तथा लक्षणसन्निपातः। एतान् हि दूते प्रवदन्ति दण्डान् वधस्तु दूतस्य न नः श्रुतोऽस्ति।।5.52.15।।
390.e: "Mutilation of limbs, flogging, shaving of the head, and deforming limbs etc. these punishments have been prescribed for an emissary. Never has killing of an emissary been heard.

390.sa: कथं च धर्मार्थविनीतबुद्धिः परावरप्रत्ययनिश्चितार्थः। भवद्विधः कोपवशे हि तिष्ठेत् कोपं नियच्छन्ति हि सत्त्ववन्तः।।5.52.16।।
390.e: "You are wellversed  in  dharma and artha. Learned men first decide what is right or wrong (before imposing punishment). How are you swayed by unjust anger? Indeed courageous persons (like you) should control anger.

390.sa: न धर्मवादे न च लोकवृत्ते न शास्त्रबुद्धिग्रहणेषु चापि। विद्येत कश्चित्तव वीर तुल्य स्त्वंह्युत्तमस्सर्वसुरासुराणाम्।।5.52.17।।
390.e: "Heroic Ravana there is hardly any one who is equal to you in the knowledge of dharma, in the practice of worldly affairs and in grasping subtle truths of sastras. Indeed you are supreme among suras and asuras.

390.sa: शूरेण वीरेण निशाचरेन्द्र सुरासुराणामपि दुर्जयेन। त्वया प्रगल्भाः सुरदैत्यसङ्घा जिताश्च युद्धेष्वसकृन्नरेन्द्राः।।5.52.18।।
390.e: "You are the king of demons. Hosts of gods and daityas efficient in wars are conquered by you again and again since you are a brave warrior invincible to gods and demons.

390.sa: न चाप्यस्य कपेर्घाते कञ्चित्पश्याम्यहं गुणम्। तेष्वयं पात्यतां दण्डो यैरयं प्रेषितः कपिः।।5.52.19।।
390.e: "I do not see any use in killing this monkey. Pronounce  punishment on those who have sent this vanara.

390.sa: साधुर्वा यदि वाऽसाधुः परैरेष समर्पितः। ब्रुवन् परार्थं परवान्न दूतो वधमर्हति।।5.52.20।।
390.e: "Whether he is soft or harsh, he has been sent by others. He is speaking on other's behalf and is dependent on them. An emissary does not deserve to be killed.

390.sa: अपि चास्मिन् हते राजन्नान्यं पश्यामि खेचरम्। इह यः पुनरागच्छेत्परं पारं महोदधेः।।5.52.21।।
390.e: "O king If he is killed, I do not see any one who can cross this great ocean and come by air to reach this place.

390.sa: तस्मान्नास्य वधे यत्नः कार्य: परपुरञ्जय। भवान् सेन्द्रेषु देवेषु यत्नमास्थातुमर्हति।।5.52.22।।
390.e: "You who can conquer citadels of enemies should not direct your efforts to kill an envoy.You are fit to make efforts against enemies like gods including Indra.

390.sa: अस्मिन्विनष्टे न हि वीरमन्यं पश्यामि यस्तौ वरराजपुत्रौ। युद्धाय युद्धप्रियदुर्विनीतावुद्योजयेद्धीर्घपथावरुद्धौ।।5.52.23।।
390.e: "O lover of war if Hanuman is slain I do not see any one who can incite those two illmannered sons of the king who are prevented from reaching this faroff land.

390.sa: पराक्रमोत्साहमनस्विनां च सुरासुराणामपि दुर्जयेन। त्वया मनोनन्दन नैतानां युद्धायतिर्नाशयतुं न युक्ता।।5.52.24।।
390.e: "O delighter of demons even the gods and demons who are endowed with valour and energy cannot win you. You are invincible. It is not proper for you to lose chances of a good war.

390.sa: हिताश्च शूराश्च समाहिताश्च कुलेषु जाताश्च महागुणेषु। मनस्विनश्शस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठाः कोट्यग्रतस्ते सुभृताश्च योधाः।।5.52.25।।
390.e: "You have with you wellwishers, courageous ones, who have good qualities born in a good race, who are noble, sensible people, wielders of weapons and wellpaid warriors in crores.

390.sa: तदेकदेशेन बलस्य तावत्केचित्तवाऽऽदेशकृतोऽभियान्तु तौ राजपुत्रौ विनिगृह्य मूढौ परेषु ते भावयितुं प्रभावम्।।5.52.26।।
390.e: By your order let some strong soldiers from one contingency go and capture the two sons of the king, to exhibit your power over the enemy.

391.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवो महात्मनः। देशकालहितं वाक्यं भ्रातुरुत्तरमब्रवीत्।।5.53.1।।
391.e: The tenheaded Ravana heard his brother, the greatsoul Vibhishana's timely advice which was in keeping with the laws of the land and replied.

391.sa: सम्यगुक्तं हि भवता दूतवध्या विगर्हिता। अवश्यं तु वधादन्यः क्रियतामस्य निग्रहः।।5.53.2।।
391.e: "Indeed, you have spoken very well.Killing of emissary is censured (in sastras). Surely we will impose suitable punishment other than killing.

391.sa: कपीनां किल लाङ्गूलमिष्टं भवति भूषणम्। तदस्य दीप्यतां शीघ्रं तेन दग्धेन गच्छतु।।5.53.3।।
391.e: "The tail is dear to the monkeys and it is an ornament for them. Set fire to it at once and let him go with his burning tail.

391.sa: ततः पश्यन्त्विमं दीनमङ्गवैरूप्यकर्शितम्। समित्रज्ञातयस्सर्वे बान्धवाः ससुहृज्जनाः।।5.53.4।। आज्ञापयद्राक्षसेन्द्रः पुरं सर्वं सचत्वरम्। लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन रक्षोभिः परिणीयताम्।।5.53.5।।
391.e: "Then all his friends, relatives and his kinsmen will see his disfigured and handicapped form. The demon king having ordered thus, the monkey was taken by the ogres round the junctions of the roads all over the city with his tail on fire.

391.sa: ततः पश्यन्त्विमं दीनमङ्गवैरूप्यकर्शितम्। समित्रज्ञातयस्सर्वे बान्धवाः ससुहृज्जनाः।।5.53.4।। आज्ञापयद्राक्षसेन्द्रः पुरं सर्वं सचत्वरम्। लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन रक्षोभिः परिणीयताम्।।5.53.5।।
391.e: "Then all his friends, relatives and his kinsmen will see his disfigured and handicapped form. The demon king having ordered thus, the monkey was taken by the ogres round the junctions of the roads all over the city with his tail on fire.

391.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसाः कोपकर्शिताः। वेष्टयन्ति स्म लाङ्गूलं जीर्णैः कार्पासकैः पटैः।।5.53.6।।
391.e: "Obeying the orders of the king, the brutally angry demons wrapped his tail with tatters of cotton.

391.sa: संवेष्ट्यमाने लाङ्गूले व्यवर्धत महाकपिः। शुष्कमिन्धनमासाद्य वनेष्विव हुताशनः।।5.53.7।।
391.e: While the tail was being swathed, the great vanara grew in size like wild fire fed with dry firewood.

391.sa: तैलेन परिषिच्याथ तेऽग्निं तत्राभ्यपातयन्। लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन राक्षसांस्तानपातयत्।।5.53.8।। रोषामर्षपरीतात्मा बालसूर्यसमाननः।
391.e: The demons soaked the tail and set fire to it. His face burning in anger shone like the rising Sun and his mind seized with indignation, he struck them with the burning tail.

391.sa: लाङ्गूलं सम्प्रदीप्तं तु द्रष्टुं तस्य हनूमतः।।5.53.9।। सहस्त्रीबालवृद्धाश्च जग्मुः प्रीता निशाचराः।
391.e: All the demons including the shedemons and their children and the elders went out joyfully to see the burning tail of Hanuman.

391.sa: स भूयः सङ्गतैः क्रूरैर्राक्षसैर्हरिसत्तमः।।5.53.10।। निबद्धः कृतवान्वीरस्तत्कालसदृशीं मतिम्।
391.e: When the cruel demons collected together and bound him once again the heroic Hanuman thought what was appropriate to the moment.

391.sa: कामं खलु न मे शक्ता निबद्धस्यापि राक्षसाः।।5.53.11।। छित्त्वा पाशान् समुत्पत्य हन्यामहमिमान्पुनः।
391.e: 'Even though these ogres are not capable, they have bound me. Indeed I will leap (into  the air) once again and sever my bonds and kill them.

391.sa: यदि भर्तुर्हितार्थाय चरन्तं भर्तृशासनात्।।5.53.12।। बध्नन्त्येते दुरात्मनो न तु मे निष्कृतिः कृता।
391.e: 'These  evilminded demons bind me, ordered by their lord. When I am moving here for the welfare of  my master, I will not let them escape৷৷

391.sa: सर्वेषामेव पर्याप्तो राक्षसानामहं युधि।।5.53.13।। किंतु रामस्य प्रीत्यर्थं विषहिष्येऽहमीदृशम्। लङ्का चारयितव्या वै पुनरेव भवेदिति।।5.53.14।।
391.e: 'I am strong enough to destroy all the demons in a battle. I am enduring this humiliation in order to make Rama happy. In this way I will get a chance to see Lanka once again.

391.sa: सर्वेषामेव पर्याप्तो राक्षसानामहं युधि।।5.53.13।। किंतु रामस्य प्रीत्यर्थं विषहिष्येऽहमीदृशम्। लङ्का चारयितव्या वै पुनरेव भवेदिति।।5.53.14।।
391.e: 'I am strong enough to destroy all the demons in a battle. I am enduring this humiliation in order to make Rama happy. In this way I will get a chance to see Lanka once again.

391.sa: रात्रौ न हि सुदृष्टा मे दुर्गकर्मविधानतः। अवश्यमेव द्रष्टव्या मया लङ्का निशाक्षये।।5.53.15।।
391.e: 'Indeed I saw Lanka at night for which I could not acquire proper knowledge about the fortification of the city. Surely it should be seen by me now after the night has passed.

391.sa: कामं बद्धस्य मे भूयः पुच्छस्योद्दीपनेन च। पीडां कुर्वन्तु रक्षांसि न मेऽस्ति मनसश्श्रमः।।5.53.16।।
391.e: 'Let the demons torture me freely by setting fire to my tail. Let them bind me. I am not exhausted.

391.sa: ततस्ते संवृताकारं सत्त्ववन्तं महाकपिम्। परिगृह्य ययुर्हृष्टा राक्षसाः कपिकुञ्जरम्।।5.53.17।।
391.e: Then the ogres set forth joyfully capturing the very powerful elephant among the monkeys, the great vanara who had contracted his body.

391.sa: शङ्खभेरीनिनादैस्तं घोषयन्तः स्वकर्मभिः। राक्षसाः क्रूरकर्माणश्चारयन्ति स्म तां पुरीम्।।5.53.18।।
391.e: The cruel demons started blowing conches and beating drums. They paraded him in the city  announcing their deeds.

391.sa: अन्वीयमानो रक्षोभिर्ययौ सुखमरिन्दमः। हनुमांश्चारयामास राक्षसानां महापुरीम्।।5.53.19।।
391.e: Hanuman, the subduer of enemies ranged forth happily while he was followed by the demons in the great city.

391.sa: अथापश्यद्विमानानि विचित्राणि महाकपिः। संवृतान् भूमिभागांश्च सुविभक्तांश्च चत्वरान्।।5.53.20।।
391.e: The great vanara saw wonderful, towering mansions, secure, mammoth buildings all over and welllaid out squares on the streets.

391.sa: वीथीश्च गृहसम्बाधाः कपिश्शृङ्गाटकानि च। तथा रथ्योपरथ्याश्च तथैव गृहकान्तरान्।।5.53.21।। गृहांश्च मेघसङ्काशान् ददर्श पवनात्मजः।
391.e: The son of the Windgod saw the streets with beautiful, tall mansions and houses appearing like clouds, highways and byways and secret routes.

391.sa: चत्वरेषु चतुष्केषु राजमार्गे तथैव च।।5.53.22।। घोषयन्ति कपिं सर्वे चारीक इति राक्षसाः।
391.e: All the demons went forth through cross roads, altars built on four pillars and royal roads announcing that he (Hanuman) was a spy.

391.sa: स्त्रीबालवृद्धाः निर्जग्मुस्तत्र तत्र कुतूहलात्।।5.53.23।। तं प्रदीपितलाङ्गूलं हनुमन्तं दिदृक्षवः।
391.e: With eagerness to have a glance at Hanuman's blazing tail, women, children and the aged here and there came out of eagerness to see him.

391.sa: दीप्यमाने ततस्तत्र लाङ्गूलाग्रे हनूमतः।।5.53.24।। राक्षस्यस्ता विरूपाक्ष्य श्शंसुर्देव्यास्तदप्रियम्।
391.e: When the tip of Hanuman's tail was set on fire, the uglyeyed shedemon. Carried the unpleasant news to divine Sita.

391.sa: यस्त्वया कृतसंवाद स्सीते ताम्रमुखः कपिः।।5.53.25।। लाङ्गूलेन प्रदीप्तेन स एष परिणीयते।
391.e: "O Sita the redfaced monkey who conversed with you is being paraded in the streets with his tail set on fire".

391.sa: श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं क्रूरमात्मापहरणोपमम्।।5.53.26।। वैदेही शोकसन्तप्ता हुताशनमुपागमत्।
391.e: Distressed on hearing the news which was as cruel as her own abduction Sita started burning with grief and invoked the firegod.

391.sa: मङ्गलाभिमुखी तस्य सा तदाऽसीन्महाकपेः।।5.53.27।। उपतस्थे विशालाक्षी प्रयता हव्यवाहनम्।
391.e: Wishing the great monkey well, the largeeyed Sita invoked the Firegod in her heart.

391.sa: यद्यस्ति पतिशुश्रूषा यद्यस्ति चरितं तपः। यदि चास्त्येकपत्नीत्वं शीतो भव हनूमतः।।5.53.28।।
391.e: "O Firegod if I have served my husband, if I have practised austerities, and if I am loyal to my husband, be cool to Hanuman.

391.sa: यदि किञ्चिदनुक्रोशस्तस्य मय्यस्ति धीमतः।।5.53.29।। यदि वा भाग्यशेषो मे शीतो भव हनूमतः।
391.e: "If wise Rama has some compassion for me, if there is any residue of good luck for me, to Hanuman be cool O Firegod.

391.sa: यदि मां वृत्तसम्पन्नां तत्समागमलालसाम्।।5.53.30।। स विजानाति धर्मात्मा शीतो भव हनूमतः।
391.e: "O Firegod if Rama is righteous, if I am pure in mind, and if I am longing to unite with him, be cool to Hanuman.

391.sa: यदि मां तारयेदार्यस्सुग्रीवः सत्यसङ्गरः।।5.53.31।। अस्माद्धुःखाम्बुसंरोधाच्छीतो भव हनूमतः।
391.e: "If Sugriva is true to his promise to fight (for me), if he should be able to rescue me from this ocean of agony let Hanuman be cool (not consumed by fire.)"

391.sa: ततस्तीक्ष्णार्चिरव्यग्रः प्रदक्षिणशिखोऽनलः।।5.53.32।। जज्वाल मृगशाबाक्ष्या श्शंसन्निव शिवं कपेः।
391.e: Then the tips of the intense flame appeared steadily moving to the fawneyed Sita indicating the firegod's auspiciousness and safety to Hanuman.

391.sa: हनुमज्जनकश्चापि पुच्छानलयुतोऽनिलः।।5.53.33।। ववौ स्वास्थ्यकरो देव्याः प्रालेयानिलशीतलः।
391.e: "The Windgod accompanying Hanuman's firelit tail also blew cool like the wind from snow, to calm the mind of the divine lady.

391.sa: दह्यमाने च लाङ्गूले चिन्तयामास वानरः।।5.53.34।। प्रदीप्तोऽग्निरयं कस्मान्न मां दहति सर्वतः।
391.e: When the tail was burning, the vanara wondered how the fire ablaze on every side was not burning him:

391.sa: दृश्यते च महाज्वालः करोति न च मे रुजम्।।5.53.35।। शिशिरस्येव सङ्घातो लाङ्गूलाग्रे प्रतिष्ठितः।
391.e: 'This huge flame is not hurting me. It  is as though a mass of ice is placed at the end of my tail. (The fire did not torture nor extend beyond the tip of my tail.)

391.sa: अथवा तदिदं व्यक्तं यद्दृष्टं प्लवता मया।।5.53.36।। रामप्रभावादाश्चर्यं पर्वत स्सरितां पतौ।
391.e: 'It must be due to the power of Rama, by which I found a wonderful mountain  emerging from the sea to give me protection while I was crossing the ocean. Now evidently this is due to Rama's power (that my tail is not burning me).

391.sa: यदि तावत्समुद्रस्य मैनाकस्य च धीमतः।।5.53.37।। रामार्थं सम्भ्रमस्तादृक्किमग्निर्न करिष्यति।
391.e: 'If the anxiety of the ocean and the wise Mainaka mountain is to serve Rama what is it that the fire cannot do?

391.sa: सीतायाश्चानृशंस्येन तेजसा राघवस्य च।।5.53.38।। पितुश्च मम सख्येन न मां दहति पावकः।
391.e: 'Because of Sita's steadfast loyalty, Rama's power and my father's friendship with the Firegod, the fire is not burning me.'

391.sa: भूयस्स चिन्तयामास मुहूर्तं कपिकुञ्जरः।।5.53.39।। उत्पपाताथ वेगेन ननाद च महाकपिः।
391.e: Once more a thought came to the great Hanuman,the elephant among monkeys. He sprang up and shouted loud.

391.sa: पुरद्वारं ततश्श्रीमान् शैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्।।5.53.40।। विभक्तरक्षस्सम्बाधमाससादानिलात्मजः।
391.e: Then the illustrious Hanuman reached the entrance of the lofty city, which was  like the peak of a mountain and turned away the demons.

391.sa: स भूत्वा शैलसङ्काशः क्षणेन पुनरात्मवान्।।5.53.41।। ह्रस्वतां परमां प्राप्तो बन्धनान्यवशातयत्।
391.e: From his mountainlike form he assumed his original small figure within a moment casting off the bonds.

391.sa: विमुक्तश्चाभवछ्रचीमान् पुनः पर्वतसन्निभः।।5.53.42।। वीक्षमाणश्च ददृशे परिघं तोरणाश्रितम्।
391.e: Illustrious Hanuman was relieved of the bond and once again grew to a mountain size. Looking around he saw an iron club near the archway.

391.sa: स तं गृह्य महाबाहुः कालायसपरिष्कृतम्।।5.53.43।। रक्षिणस्तान् पुनस्सर्वान्सूदयामास मारुतिः।
391.e: Seizing the black Iron club again, the strongarmed Hanuman killed all the demon guards.

391.sa: स तान्निहत्त्वा रणचण्डविक्रम स्समीक्षमाणः पुनरेव लङ्काम्। प्रदीप्तलाङ्गूलकृतार्चिमाली प्रकाशतादित्य इवार्चिमाली।।5.53.44।।
391.e: Hanuman, who was of fearsome valour in war with the demons, having killed them, gazed at Lanka once again. Garlanded by the flames of his tail around, he shone like the Sun covered with garlands of rays. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftythird sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

392.sa: वीक्षमाणस्ततो लङ्कां कपिः कृतमनोरथः।।5.54.1।। वर्धमानसमुत्साहः कार्यशेषमचिन्तयत्।
392.e: With his objectives achieved, the monkey gazed at Lanka with growing zeal and pondered over the remaining work.

392.sa: किन्नु खल्ववशिष्टं मे कर्तव्यमिह साम्प्रतम्।।5.54.2।। यदेषां रक्षसां भूयः सन्तापजननं भवेत्।
392.e: 'Is there anything still left which can further torment the demons here?

392.sa: वनं तावत्प्रमथितं प्रकृष्टा राक्षसा हताः।।5.54.3। बलैकदेशः क्षपितश्शेषं दुर्गविनाशनम्।
392.e: 'All the trees of the garden are broken, powerful demons have been killed, and a contingent of the army is destroyed. Only the destruction of the citadel is left.

392.sa: दुर्गे विनाशिते कर्म भवेत्सुखपरिश्रमम्। अल्पयत्नेन कार्येऽस्मिन् मम स्यात्सफलश्श्रमः।।5.54.4।।
392.e: 'If the citadel is destroyed it would be a happy conclusion with a little effort. I can successfully complete my task.

392.sa: यो ह्ययं मम लाङ्गूले दीप्यते हव्यवाहनः। अस्य सन्तर्पणं न्याय्यं कर्तुमेभिर्गृहोत्तमैः।।5.54.5।।
392.e: 'It would be proper to satiate this fire at the end of my tail  by offering it to these excellent mansions (I shall set fire to these houses).

392.sa: ततः प्रदीप्तलाङ्गूलस्सविद्युदिव तोयदः। भवनाग्रेषु लङ्काया विचचार महाकपिः।।5.54.6।।
392.e: The great Hanuman, with his burning tail wandered on tops of the mansions of Lanka, which looked like clouds with lightning.

392.sa: गृहाद्गृहं राक्षसानामुद्यानानि च वानरः। वीक्षमाणो ह्यसन्त्रस्तः प्रासादांश्च चचार सः।।5.54.7।।
392.e: The vanara moved from one house to the other, looking at the gardens and houses of the demons without fear.

392.sa: अवप्लुत्य महावेगः प्रहस्तस्य निवेशनम्। अग्निं तत्र स निक्षिप्य श्वसनेन समो बली।।5.54.8।। ततोऽन्यत्पुप्लुवे वेश्म महापार्श्वस्य वीर्यवान्। मुमोच हनुमानग्निं कालानलशिखोपमम्।।5.54.9।।
392.e: Powerful and brave Hanuman who was equal to the Windgod in speed jumped down on the house of Prahasta and set fire to it. From there he jumped on to Mahaparsva's house and set it ablaze. Hanuman appeared like the fireflame at the time of dissolution.

392.sa: अवप्लुत्य महावेगः प्रहस्तस्य निवेशनम्। अग्निं तत्र स निक्षिप्य श्वसनेन समो बली।।5.54.8।। ततोऽन्यत्पुप्लुवे वेश्म महापार्श्वस्य वीर्यवान्। मुमोच हनुमानग्निं कालानलशिखोपमम्।।5.54.9।।
392.e: Powerful and brave Hanuman who was equal to the Windgod in speed jumped down on the house of Prahasta and set fire to it. From there he jumped on to Mahaparsva's house and set it ablaze. Hanuman appeared like the fireflame at the time of dissolution.

392.sa: वज्रदंष्ट्रस्य च तदा पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः। शुकस्य च महातेजास्सारणस्य च धीमतः।।5.54.10।।
392.e: The great, brilliant vanara bounded on to Vajradamstra's, of Suka's and wise Sarana's.

392.sa: तथा चेन्द्रजितो वेश्म ददाह हरियूथपः। जम्बुमाले स्सुमालेश्च ददाह भवनं ततः।।5.54.11।।
392.e: Thus Hanuman, the chief of the vanaras set fire to Indrajit's residence and then to Jambumali's and Sumali's building.

392.sa: रश्मिकेतोश्च भवनं सूर्यशत्रोस्तथैव च। ह्रस्वकर्णस्य दंष्ट्रस्य रोमशस्य च रक्षसः।।5.54.12।। युद्धोन्मत्तस्य मत्तस्य ध्वजग्रीवस्य रक्षसः। विद्युज्जिह्वस्य घोरस्य तथा हस्तिमुखस्य च।।5.54.13।। करालस्य पिशाचस्य शोणिताक्षस्य चैव हि। कुम्भकर्णस्य भवनं मकराक्षस्य चैव हि।।5.54.14।। यज्ञशत्रोश्च भवनं ब्रह्मशत्रोस्तथैव च। नरान्तकस्य कुम्भस्य निकुम्भस्य दुरात्मनः।।5.54.15।। वर्जयित्वा महातेजा विभीषणगृहं प्रति। क्रममाणः क्रमेणैव ददाह हरिपुङ्गवः।।5.54.16।।
392.e: The brilliant monkey leader bypassed Vibhishanas's house and avoiding it that way set fire to the mansions of other ogres, Rasmiketu, Suryasatru, Hrasvakarna, Vajradamshtra, Romasa, Yuddhonmatta, Matta, Dhwajagriva, Vidyujjihva, Hastimukha, Karala, Pisacha, Sonitaksha, Kumbhakarna, Makaraksha, Yagnasatru, Brahmasatru, Naranthaka, Kumbha, and wicked Nikumbha.

392.sa: रश्मिकेतोश्च भवनं सूर्यशत्रोस्तथैव च। ह्रस्वकर्णस्य दंष्ट्रस्य रोमशस्य च रक्षसः।।5.54.12।। युद्धोन्मत्तस्य मत्तस्य ध्वजग्रीवस्य रक्षसः। विद्युज्जिह्वस्य घोरस्य तथा हस्तिमुखस्य च।।5.54.13।। करालस्य पिशाचस्य शोणिताक्षस्य चैव हि। कुम्भकर्णस्य भवनं मकराक्षस्य चैव हि।।5.54.14।। यज्ञशत्रोश्च भवनं ब्रह्मशत्रोस्तथैव च। नरान्तकस्य कुम्भस्य निकुम्भस्य दुरात्मनः।।5.54.15।। वर्जयित्वा महातेजा विभीषणगृहं प्रति। क्रममाणः क्रमेणैव ददाह हरिपुङ्गवः।।5.54.16।।
392.e: The brilliant monkey leader bypassed Vibhishanas's house and avoiding it that way set fire to the mansions of other ogres, Rasmiketu, Suryasatru, Hrasvakarna, Vajradamshtra, Romasa, Yuddhonmatta, Matta, Dhwajagriva, Vidyujjihva, Hastimukha, Karala, Pisacha, Sonitaksha, Kumbhakarna, Makaraksha, Yagnasatru, Brahmasatru, Naranthaka, Kumbha, and wicked Nikumbha.

392.sa: रश्मिकेतोश्च भवनं सूर्यशत्रोस्तथैव च। ह्रस्वकर्णस्य दंष्ट्रस्य रोमशस्य च रक्षसः।।5.54.12।। युद्धोन्मत्तस्य मत्तस्य ध्वजग्रीवस्य रक्षसः। विद्युज्जिह्वस्य घोरस्य तथा हस्तिमुखस्य च।।5.54.13।। करालस्य पिशाचस्य शोणिताक्षस्य चैव हि। कुम्भकर्णस्य भवनं मकराक्षस्य चैव हि।।5.54.14।। यज्ञशत्रोश्च भवनं ब्रह्मशत्रोस्तथैव च। नरान्तकस्य कुम्भस्य निकुम्भस्य दुरात्मनः।।5.54.15।। वर्जयित्वा महातेजा विभीषणगृहं प्रति। क्रममाणः क्रमेणैव ददाह हरिपुङ्गवः।।5.54.16।।
392.e: The brilliant monkey leader bypassed Vibhishanas's house and avoiding it that way set fire to the mansions of other ogres, Rasmiketu, Suryasatru, Hrasvakarna, Vajradamshtra, Romasa, Yuddhonmatta, Matta, Dhwajagriva, Vidyujjihva, Hastimukha, Karala, Pisacha, Sonitaksha, Kumbhakarna, Makaraksha, Yagnasatru, Brahmasatru, Naranthaka, Kumbha, and wicked Nikumbha.

392.sa: रश्मिकेतोश्च भवनं सूर्यशत्रोस्तथैव च। ह्रस्वकर्णस्य दंष्ट्रस्य रोमशस्य च रक्षसः।।5.54.12।। युद्धोन्मत्तस्य मत्तस्य ध्वजग्रीवस्य रक्षसः। विद्युज्जिह्वस्य घोरस्य तथा हस्तिमुखस्य च।।5.54.13।। करालस्य पिशाचस्य शोणिताक्षस्य चैव हि। कुम्भकर्णस्य भवनं मकराक्षस्य चैव हि।।5.54.14।। यज्ञशत्रोश्च भवनं ब्रह्मशत्रोस्तथैव च। नरान्तकस्य कुम्भस्य निकुम्भस्य दुरात्मनः।।5.54.15।। वर्जयित्वा महातेजा विभीषणगृहं प्रति। क्रममाणः क्रमेणैव ददाह हरिपुङ्गवः।।5.54.16।।
392.e: The brilliant monkey leader bypassed Vibhishanas's house and avoiding it that way set fire to the mansions of other ogres, Rasmiketu, Suryasatru, Hrasvakarna, Vajradamshtra, Romasa, Yuddhonmatta, Matta, Dhwajagriva, Vidyujjihva, Hastimukha, Karala, Pisacha, Sonitaksha, Kumbhakarna, Makaraksha, Yagnasatru, Brahmasatru, Naranthaka, Kumbha, and wicked Nikumbha.

392.sa: रश्मिकेतोश्च भवनं सूर्यशत्रोस्तथैव च। ह्रस्वकर्णस्य दंष्ट्रस्य रोमशस्य च रक्षसः।।5.54.12।। युद्धोन्मत्तस्य मत्तस्य ध्वजग्रीवस्य रक्षसः। विद्युज्जिह्वस्य घोरस्य तथा हस्तिमुखस्य च।।5.54.13।। करालस्य पिशाचस्य शोणिताक्षस्य चैव हि। कुम्भकर्णस्य भवनं मकराक्षस्य चैव हि।।5.54.14।। यज्ञशत्रोश्च भवनं ब्रह्मशत्रोस्तथैव च। नरान्तकस्य कुम्भस्य निकुम्भस्य दुरात्मनः।।5.54.15।। वर्जयित्वा महातेजा विभीषणगृहं प्रति। क्रममाणः क्रमेणैव ददाह हरिपुङ्गवः।।5.54.16।।
392.e: The brilliant monkey leader bypassed Vibhishanas's house and avoiding it that way set fire to the mansions of other ogres, Rasmiketu, Suryasatru, Hrasvakarna, Vajradamshtra, Romasa, Yuddhonmatta, Matta, Dhwajagriva, Vidyujjihva, Hastimukha, Karala, Pisacha, Sonitaksha, Kumbhakarna, Makaraksha, Yagnasatru, Brahmasatru, Naranthaka, Kumbha, and wicked Nikumbha.

392.sa: तेषु तेषु महार्हेषु भवनेषु महायशाः। गृहेष्वृद्धिमतामृद्धिं ददाह स महाकपिः।।5.54.17।।
392.e: Moving among those highly luxurious mansions the glorious Vanara burnt away the wealth of all the rich demons.

392.sa: सर्वेषां समतिक्रम्य राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वीर्यवान्। आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान् रावणस्य निवेशनम्।।5.54.18।।
392.e: Heroic and illustrious Hanuman, having crossed all the residences of the ogres finally reached the palace of Ravana, the king.

392.sa: ततस्तस्मिन्गृहे मुख्ये नानारत्नविभूषिते। मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशे सर्वमङ्गळशोभिते।।5.54.19।। प्रदीप्तमग्निमुत्सृज्य लाङ्गूलाग्रे प्रतिष्ठितम्। ननाद हनुमान्वीरो युगान्तजलदो यथा।।5.54.20।।
392.e: Then Hanuman, the hero with the burning tail set fire to the chief palace of Ravana that resembled mountains Meru and Mandara, decorated with different kinds of gems and exquisite with several auspicious articles. While the flames were rising up, he roared like the thundering cloud at the time of dissolution.

392.sa: ततस्तस्मिन्गृहे मुख्ये नानारत्नविभूषिते। मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशे सर्वमङ्गळशोभिते।।5.54.19।। प्रदीप्तमग्निमुत्सृज्य लाङ्गूलाग्रे प्रतिष्ठितम्। ननाद हनुमान्वीरो युगान्तजलदो यथा।।5.54.20।।
392.e: Then Hanuman, the hero with the burning tail set fire to the chief palace of Ravana that resembled mountains Meru and Mandara, decorated with different kinds of gems and exquisite with several auspicious articles. While the flames were rising up, he roared like the thundering cloud at the time of dissolution.

392.sa: श्वसनेन च संयोगादतिवेगो महाबलः। कालाग्निरिव जज्वाल प्रावर्धत हुताशनः।।5.54.21।।
392.e: The windgod's association made the fire spread at great speed. It appeared like fire at the time of dissolution.

392.sa: प्रदीप्तमग्निं पवनस्तेषु वेश्मस्वचारयत्। अभूच्छ्वसनसंयोगादतिवेगो हुताशनः।।5.54.22।।
392.e: Combined with the wind the fire began to spread, burning the houses with great speed.

392.sa: तानि काञ्चनजालानि मुक्तामणिमयानि च। भवनान्यवशीर्यन्त रत्नवन्ति महान्ति च।।5.54.23।।
392.e: The palatial structures with windows of golden meshwork, embedded with pearls and gems and other precious stones tumbled.

392.sa: संजज्ञे तुमुलश्शब्दो राक्षसानां प्रधावताम्। स्वगृहस्य परित्राणे भग्नोत्साहोर्जितश्रियाम्।।5.54.24।। नूनमेषोऽग्निरायातः कपिरूपेण हा इति।
392.e: Unable to protect their rich houses, and thoroughly disappointed the demons said, 'Alas, the Firegod came in the form of a vanara' A tumultuous sound arose.

392.sa: क्रन्दन्त्यस्सहसा पेतुः स्तनन्धयधराः स्त्रियः।।5.54.25।। काश्चिदग्निपरीतेभ्यो हर्मेभ्यो मुक्तमूर्धजाः। पतन्त्यो रेजिरेऽभ्रेभ्यस्सौदामन्य इवाम्बरात्।।5.54.26।।
392.e: A few shedemons at once jumped out of their burning mansions surrounded by fire. They held their breastfeeding babies in their arms, their hair let loose shouting as they jumped. As they were alighting, they glowed like lightnings dropping from the clouds.

392.sa: क्रन्दन्त्यस्सहसा पेतुः स्तनन्धयधराः स्त्रियः।।5.54.25।। काश्चिदग्निपरीतेभ्यो हर्मेभ्यो मुक्तमूर्धजाः। पतन्त्यो रेजिरेऽभ्रेभ्यस्सौदामन्य इवाम्बरात्।।5.54.26।।
392.e: A few shedemons at once jumped out of their burning mansions surrounded by fire. They held their breastfeeding babies in their arms, their hair let loose shouting as they jumped. As they were alighting, they glowed like lightnings dropping from the clouds.

392.sa: वज्रविद्रुमवैदूर्यमुक्तारजतसंहितान्। विचित्रान्भवनाद्धातून् स्यन्दमानान्ददर्श सः।।5.54.27।।
392.e: Hanuman saw many colourful molten minerals mixed with diamonds, corals vaiduryas, pearls and silver flowing (dropping) from every mansion.

392.sa: नाग्निस्तृप्यति काष्ठानां तृणानां च यथा तथा। हनूमान् राक्षसेन्दाणां विशस्तानां न तृप्यति।।5.54.28।।
392.e: Just as fire is not satisfied with dry sticks and grass Hanuman was not satisfied with the dead demons.

392.sa: क्वचित्किंशुकसङ्काशाः क्वचिच्छाल्मलिसन्निभाः।।5.54.29।। क्वचित्कुङ्कुमसङ्काशाश्शिखा वह्नेश्चकाशिरे।
392.e: The flames of fire were shining like kimsuka flowers here, like salmali wood there, and like saffron flowers elsewhere.

392.sa: हनूमता वेगवता वानरेण महात्मना। लङ्कापुरं प्रदग्धं तद्रुद्रेण त्रिपुरं यथा।।5.54.30।।
392.e: Hanuman, endowed with great speed, burnt Lanka just as Tripurari, or Rudra burnt theTripuras (three cities of gold, silver and iron).

392.sa: ततस्तु लङ्कापुरपर्वताग्रे समुत्थितो भीमपराक्रमोऽग्निः। प्रसार्य चूडावलयं प्रदीप्तो हनूमता वेगवता विसृष्टः।।5.54.31।।
392.e: The fierce fire lit by Hanuman, the hero endowed with great speed, spread around in circles and shot up flying high to the top of the Trikuta mountain on which Lanka was located.

392.sa: युगान्तकालानलतुल्यवेग स्समारुतोऽग्निर्ववृधे दिविस्पृक्। विधूमरश्मिर्भवनेषु सक्तो रक्षश्शरीराज्यसमर्पतार्चिः।।5.54.32।।
392.e: Fanned by the wind, inflamed by the fat from the corpses of the demons, the fire spread in the mansions burning without smoke. It spread with great speed like the fire at the end of the universe.

392.sa: आदित्यकोटीसदृशस्सुतेजा लङ्कां समस्तां परिवार्य तिष्ठन्। शब्दैरनेकैरशनिप्ररूढैर्भिन्दन्निवाण्डं प्रबभौ महाग्निः।।5.54.33।।
392.e: The highly radiant fire stood like a crore of Suns surrounding the entire Lanka. It was glowing, cracking like Indra's thunderbolt as though the whole universe was collapsing.

392.sa: तत्राम्बरादग्निरतिप्रवृद्धो रूक्षप्रभः किंशुकपुष्पचूडः। निर्वाणधूमाकुलराजयश्च नीलोत्पलाभाः प्रचकाशिरेऽभ्राः।।5.54.34।।
392.e: The dazzling flames of fire red like kimsuka flowers shot up violently into the sky. The clouds engulfed by the smoke rising from the subsiding fire was shining like the lustre of blue lotuses .

392.sa: वज्री महेन्द्रस्त्रिदशेश्वरो वा साक्षाद्यमो वा वरुणोऽनिलो वा। रुद्रोऽग्निरर्को धनदश्च सोमो न वानरोऽयं स्वयमेव कालः।।5.54.35।।
392.e: 'Is this the wielder of thunderbolt Indra, who is the king of gods? Is it Yama himself? Is It the Windgod, or Firegod, or Varuna or Rudra? Is it Kubera or Sun or Moon or is it the god of death himself? He cannot be a mere monkey, indeed.

392.sa: किं ब्रह्मणस्सर्वपितामहस्य सर्वस्य धातुश्चतुराननस्य। इहाऽऽगतो वानररूपधारी रक्षोपसंहारकरः प्रकोपः।।5.54.36।।
392.e: 'Or is it Grandfather Brahma, the supreme fourfaced god enraged and arrived in the form of vanara to kill the clan of demons?

392.sa: किं वैष्णवं वा कपिरूपमेत्य रक्षोविनाशाय परं सुतेजः। अनन्तमव्यक्तमचिन्त्यमेकं स्वमायया साम्प्रतमागतं वा।।5.54.37।।
392.e: 'Can he be the vast boundless energy, the unthinkable and infinite lord Visnu assuming the monkeyform? Is he the peerless, unmanifest form beyond all imagination who has arrived here by virtue of his Maya (illusory power) in order to destroy the demons'?

392.sa: इत्येवमूचुर्बहवो विशिष्टा रक्षोगणास्तत्र समेत्य सर्वे। सप्राणिसङ्घां सगृहां सवृक्षां दग्धां पुरीं तां सहसा समीक्ष्य।।5.54.38।।
392.e: All eminent demons having collected together, quickly surveyed the situation.Seeing the burnt city, with  all its living creatures, houses and trees consigned to the flames, they spoke to one another.

392.sa: ततस्तु लङ्का सहसा प्रदग्धा सराक्षसा साश्वरथा सनागा। सपक्षिसङ्घा समृगा सवृक्षा रुरोद दीना तुमुलं सशब्दम्।।5.54.39।।
392.e: Lanka with its chariots horses, elephants, flocks of birds, animals and trees burnt all of a sudden, the ogres cried loudly and piteously.

392.sa: हा तात हा पुत्रक कान्त मित्र हा जीवितं भोगयुतं सुपुण्यम्। रक्षोभिरेवं बहुधा ब्रुवद्भि श्शब्दः कृतो घोरतरस्सुभीमः।।5.54.40।।
392.e: "O father dear O son O my dear O friend alas, the life which is enjoyable, sacred and prosperous is destroyed in this way". Saying this, the demons cried out dreadfully and loudly.

392.sa: हुताशनज्वालसमावृता सा हतप्रवीरा परिवृत्तयोधा हनूमतः क्रोधबलाभिभूता बभूव शापोपहतेव लङ्का।।5.54.41।।
392.e: With the Fire god spreading flames all over, heroes dead, retreating troops shattered by Hanuman's anger, Lanka appeared as though it was cursed.

392.sa: स सम्भ्रमत्रस्तविषण्णराक्षसां समुज्ज्वलज्ज्वालहुताशनाङ्किताम्। ददर्श लङ्कां हनुमान्महामनाः स्वयम्भूकोपोपहतामिवावनिम्।।5.54.42।।
392.e: Highly sensitive Hanuman saw the city of Lanka filled with perplexed, scared and sorrowful demons, Lanka succumbed to the flames of firegod and looked as if it was  hit by the anger of Brahma, the selfborn god.

392.sa: भङ्क्त्वा वनं पादपरत्नसङ्कुलं हत्वा तु रक्षांसि महान्ति संयुगे। दग्ध्वा पुरीं तां गृहरत्नमालिनीं तस्थौ हनूमान्पवनात्मजः कपिः।।5.54.43।।
392.e: Hanuman, son of the Windgod stood at ease having shattered the garden that was full of excellent trees, and killed the demons and burnt down rows of beautiful houses in the city.

392.sa: त्रिकूटशृङ्गाग्रतले विचित्रे प्रतिष्ठितो वानरराजसिंहः। प्रदीप्तलाङ्गूलकृतार्चिमाली व्यराजताऽऽदित्य इवांशुमाली।।5.54.44।।
392.e: Standing on the peak of Trikuta mountain with his tail burning like the aura of the Sun, the lion among vanaras looked resplendent like the Sun surrounded by his rays.

392.sa: स राक्षसांस्तान्सुबहूंश्च हत्वा वनं च भङ्क्त्वा बहुपादपं तत्। विसृज्य रक्षोभवनेषु चाग्निं जगाम रामं मनसा महात्मा।।5.54.45।।
392.e: Great Hanuman, sought Rama's presence in his mind after killing many demons, breaking down many trees of the garden, and setting fire to the mansions of demons.

392.sa: ततस्तु तं वानरवीरमुख्यं महाबलं मारुततुल्यवेगम्। महामतिं वायुसुतं वरिष्ठं प्रतुष्टुवुर्देवगणाश्च सर्वे।।5.54.46।।
392.e: All the gods praised the vanara chief, son of the Windgod, who was powerful, wise and efficient and had the speed of the Wind.

392.sa: भङ्क्त्वा वनं महातेजा हत्वा रक्षांसि संयुगे। दग्ध्वा लङ्कापुरीं रम्यां रराज स महाकपिः।।5.54.47।।
392.e: Hanuman destroyed the garden, killed the demons, burnt the city of Lanka and was shining with delight

392.sa: तत्र देवास्सगन्धर्वास्सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। दृष्ट्वा लङ्कां प्रदग्धां तां विस्मयं परमं गताः।।5.54.48।।
392.e: The gandharvas, gods, siddhas and great sages were amazed at seeing the burning city of Lanka৷৷

392.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा वानरश्रेष्ठं हनुमन्तं महाकपिम्। कालाग्निरिति सञ्चिन्त्य सर्वभूतानि तत्रसुः।।5.54.49।।
392.e: All beings were afraid of Hanuman thinking that he was the fatal fire, consuming worlds at the hour of dissolution .

392.sa: देवाश्च सर्वे मुनिपुङ्गवाश्च गन्धर्वविद्याधरनागयक्षाः। भूतानि सर्वाणि महान्ति तत्र जग्मुः परां प्रीतिमतुल्यरूपाम्।।5.54.50।।
392.e: All gods, great sages, gandharvas, vidyadharas, nagas and yakshas and all great beings experienced supreme joy. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfourth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

393.sa: लङ्कां समस्तां सन्दीप्य लाङ्गूलाग्निं महाबलः। निर्वापयामास तदा समुद्रे हरिसत्तमः।। सन्दीप्यमानां विध्वस्तां त्रस्तरक्षोगणां पुरीम्। आवेक्ष्य हनुमान् लङ्कां चिन्तयामास वानरः।।5.55.1।।
393.e: Powerful Hanuman, having burnt the entire city of Lanka, put out the fire on his tail in the ocean. Beholding the burning city, the destroyed gardens and the panic stricken ogres, he began to think:

393.sa: तस्याभूत्सुमहांस्त्रासः कुत्सा चात्मन्यजायत। लङ्कां प्रदहता कर्म किंस्वित्कृतमिदं मया।।5.55.2।।
393.e: Overtaken by great fear, Hanuman felt a sense of selfreproach seeing Lanka reduced to ashes, and said, ' Lanka is burnt. What a heinous action has been perpetrated by me'.

393.sa: धन्यास्ते पुरुषश्रेष्ठा ये बुद्ध्या कोपमुत्थितम्। निरुन्धन्ति महात्मानो दीप्तमग्निमिवाम्भसा।।5.55.3।।
393.e: 'Blessed indeed are the highsouled men, who in their wisdom restrain their own anger as one would put off  burning fire with water.

393.sa: क्रुद्धः पापं न कुर्यात्कः क्रुद्धो हन्याद्गुरूनपि। क्रुद्धः परुषया वाचा नरस्साधूनधिक्षिपेत्।।5.55.4।।
393.e: 'Which sinful act an angry man will not commit? He will even kill his respectable elders or insult sages with his harsh tongue.

393.sa: वाच्यावाच्यं प्रकुपितो न विजानाति कर्हिचित्। नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते क्वचित्।।5.55.5।।
393.e: 'An angry person knows not what he should utter and what he should not. No act appears wrong for an angry man. Nothing is unutterable for him at any time, anywhere.

393.sa: यस्समुत्पतितं क्रोधं क्षमयैव निरस्यति। यथोरगस्त्वचं जीर्णां स वै पुरुष उच्यते।।5.55.6।।
393.e: 'A man who drives away his rising anger with tolerance just as a snake casts off its slough is alone called a truly wise man.

393.sa: धिगस्तु मां सुदुर्बुद्धिं निर्लज्जं पापकृत्तमम्। अचिन्तयित्वा तां सीतामग्निदं स्वामिघातुकम्।।5.55.7।।
393.e: 'Fie upon me, a wicked, shameless person and the greatest sinner for betraying the  master and setting fire to the city without thinking of Sita.

393.sa: यदि दग्धा त्वियं लङ्का नूनमार्याऽपि जानकी। दग्धा तेन मया भर्तुर्हितं कार्यमजानता।।5.55.8।।
393.e: 'If this Lanka is burnt, even noble Janaki is burnt, my master's work is spoilt by me unknowingly.

393.sa: यदर्थमयमारम्भस्तत्कार्यमवसादितम्। मया हि दहता लङ्कां न सीता परिरक्षिता।।5.55.9।।
393.e: 'My very mission is foiled. Sita has not been protected by me for no part of Lanka has escaped unburnt.

393.sa: ईषत्कार्यमिदं कार्यं कृतमासीन्न संशयः। तस्य क्रोधाभिभूतेन मया मूलक्षयः कृतः।।5.55.10।।
393.e: 'A small work is done, no doubt. But the very root of my achievement has been destroyed in my anger.

393.sa: विनष्टा जानकी नूनं न ह्यदग्धः प्रदृश्यते। लङ्कायां कश्चिदुद्धेशस्सर्वा भस्मीकृता पुरी।।5.55.11।।
393.e: 'Surely Janaki has perished in Lanka, for not even a little place is left unburnt. The entire city is reduced to ashes.

393.sa: यदि तद्विहतं कार्यं मम प्रज्ञाविपर्ययात्। इहैव प्राणसंन्यासो ममापि ह्यद्य रोचते।।5.55.12।।
393.e: 'If my work has been destroyed by my perversity of judgement, I will give up my life now  and here itself'.

393.sa: किमग्नौ निपताम्यद्य आहोस्विद्बडबामुखे। शरीरमाहो सत्त्वानां दद्मि सागरवासिनाम्।।5.55.13।।
393.e: 'Shall I end my life by jumping into fire just now, or else into the mouth of submarine fire? Should I offer my body to the living creatures of the ocean as their food?

393.sa: कथं हि जीवता शक्यो मया द्रष्टुं हरीश्वरः। तौ वा पुरुषशार्दूलौ कार्यसर्वस्वघातिना।।5.55.14।।
393.e: 'Having spoilt the entire work how can I show my face to the king of monkeys? How is it possible to see both the tigers among men?

393.sa: मया खलु तदेवेदं रोषदोषात्प्रदर्शितम्। प्रथितं त्रिषु लोकेषु कपित्वमनवस्थितम्।।5.55.15।।
393.e: 'On account of my mistake of yielding to anger, I have exhibited the unstable monkeynature and made it well established in the three worlds.

393.sa: धिगस्तु राजसं भावमनीशमनवस्थितम्। ईश्वरेणापि यद्रागान्मया सीता न रक्षिता।।5.55.16।।
393.e: 'Fie upon my hasty action commited due to lack of selfcontrol. I did not save Sita eventhough the entire situation was under my control. (I had the  capacity to save her. But I failed due to anger.)

393.sa: विनष्टायां तु सीतायां तावुभौ विनशिष्यतः। तयोर्विनाशे सुग्रीवः सबन्धुर्विनशिष्यति।।5.55.17।।
393.e: 'If the two princes know about Sita's loss they will die and when they are dead Sugriva would perish along with all his relatives.

393.sa: एतदेव वचश्श्रुत्वा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। धर्मात्मा सहशत्रुघ्नः कथं शक्ष्यति जीवितुम्।।5.55.18।।
393.e: 'How will the loving righteous brother, Bharata along with Satrughna survive after hearing this?

393.sa: इक्ष्वाकुवंशे धर्मिष्ठे गते नाशमसंशयम्। भविष्यन्ति प्रजास्सर्वाश्शोकसन्तापपीडिताः।।5.55.19।।
393.e: 'When the righteous Ikshvaku race perishes the people would be tormented by grief and remorse. There is no doubt.

393.sa: तदहं भाग्यरहितो लुप्तधर्मार्थसङ्ग्रहः।।5.55.20।। रोषदोषपरीतात्मा व्यक्तं लोकविनाशनः।
393.e: 'I have failed in seeking dharma and artha. It is evident is that I am a destroyer of the world because I was overtaken by anger. How unfortunate I am'

393.sa: इति चिन्तयतस्तस्य निमित्तान्युपपेदिरे। पूर्वमप्युपलब्धानि साक्षात्पुनरचिन्तयत्।।5.55.21।।
393.e: When Hanuman was thus bemoaning, good omens as in the past appeared before him. He started reflecting once again:

393.sa: अथवा चारुसर्वाङ्गी रक्षिता स्वेन तेजसा। न नशिष्यति कल्याणी नाग्निरग्नौ प्रवर्तते।।5.55.22।।
393.e: 'On the other hand a beautiful and auspicious lady like Sita will be protected by her own splendour and will not perish as fire cannot extinguish fire. (Sita is pure like fire. Here the great sage Valmiki is suggesting the future incident in which Sita emerged safe from 'Agnipariksha' or fireordeal.)

393.sa: न हि धर्मात्मनस्तस्य भार्याममिततेजसः। स्वचारित्राभिगुप्तां तां स्प्रष्टुमर्हति पावकः।।5.55.23।।
393.e: 'Fire cannot touch that lady who is protected by her own chastity and who is wedded to the righteous man of immasureable glory.

393.sa: नूनं रामप्रभावेण वैदेह्यास्सुकृतेन च। यन्मां दहनकर्मायं नादहद्धव्यवाहनः।।5.55.24।।
393.e: 'Fire, the consumer of oblations who has the property of burning has not burnt me and this is surely on account of Rama's power and Vaidehi's merits.

393.sa: त्रयाणां भरतादीनां भ्रात्रूणां देवता च या। रामस्य च मन: कान्ता सा कथं विनशिष्यति।।5.55.25।।
393.e: 'To Bharata, Lakshmana and Satrughna she is a goddess and she is dear to Rama's heart, how would she perish?

393.sa: यद्वा दहनकर्मायं सर्वत्र प्रभुरव्ययः। न मे दहति लाङ्गूलं कथमार्यां प्रधक्ष्यति।।5.55.26।
393.e: 'If not so, the firegod who never fails in burning has not burnt my tail. How will he burn noble Sita?'

393.sa: पुनश्चाचिन्तयत्तत्र हनुमान्विस्मितस्तदा। हिरण्यनाभस्य गिरेर्जलमध्ये प्रदर्शनम्।।5.55.27।।
393.e: Then Hanuman thought of the appearance of mountain Hiranyanabha in the midst of water, a wonderful phenomenon.

393.sa: तपसा सत्यवाक्येन अनन्यत्वाच्च भर्तरि। अपि सा निर्दहेदग्निं न तामग्निः प्रधक्ष्यति।।5.55.28।।
393.e: 'By virtue of her power of asceticism, power of truthfulness and exclusive devotion towards her husband, she may consume the fire. Fire will not burn her'.

393.sa: स तथा चिन्तयंस्तत्र देव्या धर्मपरिग्रहम्। शुश्राव हनुमान्वाक्यं चारणानां महात्मनाम्।।5.55.29।।
393.e: As Hanuman was thinking so, he heard the words of the great charanas who were praising the queen's power of righteousness.

393.sa: अहो खलु कृतं कर्म दुष्करं हि हनूमता। अग्निं विसृजताऽभीक्ष्णं भीमं राक्षसवेश्मनि।।5.55.30।।
393.e: 'Oh Hanuman has indeed accomplished the marvellous task of spreading the terrific fire on the demons buildings.

393.sa: प्रपलायितरक्षः स्त्रीबालवृद्धसमाकुला। जनकोलाहलाध्माता क्रन्दन्तीवाद्रिकन्दरै: ।।5.55.31।।
393.e: The city is crowded with women, children and old demons running (in a bid to save themselves). The loud wails of demons resounded in the mountaincaves. It was as if the city was shrieking loudly.

393.sa: दग्धेयं नगरी सर्वा साट्टप्राकारतोरणा। जानकी न च दग्धेति विस्मयोऽद्भुत एव नः।।5.55.32।।
393.e: 'The city with its towering markets, ramparts and portals is burnt, but Janaki is not. It is really wonderful, strange

393.sa: स निमित्तैश्च दृष्टार्थैः कारणैश्च महागुणैः। ऋषिवाक्यैश्च हनुमानभवत्प्रीतमानसः।।5.55.33।।
393.e: With omens that proved to be right and for good reasons and from the words of the sages (charanas), Hanuman felt happy.

393.sa: ततः कपिः प्राप्तमनोरथार्थस्तामक्षतां राजसुतां विदित्वा। प्रत्यक्षतस्तां पुनरेव दृष्टवा प्रतिप्रयाणाय मतिं चकार।।5.55.34।।
393.e: Hanuman, having fulfilled his desires and knowing that Sita is not hurt, thought of departing after meeting Sita once again (to testify that she is really safe). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfifth sarga of Sundarakanda  of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

394.sa: ततस्तु शिंशुपामूले जानकीं पर्युपस्थिताम्। अभिवाद्याब्रवीद्दिष्ट्या पश्यामि त्वामिहाक्षताम्।।5.56.1।।
394.e: Then Hanuman offered salutations to Janaki, stationed at the foot of the simsupa tree, and said, "Luckily I see you unscathed."

394.sa: ततस्तं प्रस्थितं सीता वीक्षमाणा पुनः पुनः। भर्तृस्नेहान्वितं वाक्यं हनुमन्तमभाषत।।5.56.2।।
394.e: Looking at Hanuman again and again, as he was ready to start on his return journey, thus spoke Sita expressing her love for her husband:

394.sa: काममस्य त्वमेवैकः कार्यस्य परिसाधने। पर्याप्तः परवीरघ्न यशस्यस्ते बलोदयः।।5.56.3।।
394.e: "O destroyer of foes, you are capable of rescuing me singlehanded. Your success will  raise your strength and bring glory.

394.sa: शरैस्तु सङ्कुलां कृत्वा लङ्कां परबलार्दनः। मां नयेद्यदि काकुत्स्थस्तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्।।5.56.4।।
394.e: "If Kakutstha Rama, the slayer of enemy forces comes to Lanka, fills it with his arrows and takes me back, it will be worthy of him.

394.sa: तद्यथा तस्य विक्रान्तमनुरूपं महात्मनः। भवत्याहवशूरस्य तथा त्वमुपपादय।।5.56.5।।
394.e: "You should act in such a manner that the exalted Rama, who is chivalrous in the battlefield, exhibits his valour worthy of his stature".

394.sa: तदर्थोपहितं वाक्यं प्रश्रितं हेतुसंहितम्। निशम्य हनुमांस्तस्या वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्।।5.56.6।।
394.e: Hearing her meaningful reply which was welldisposed and reasonable, Hanuman replied:

394.sa: क्षिप्रमेष्यति काकुत्स्थः हर्यृक्षप्रवरैर्वृतः। यस्ते युधि विजित्यारीन् शोकं व्यपनयिष्यति।।5.56.7।।
394.e: "Rama will come soon with the best of vanaras and bears. He would win the battle and remove your sorrrow.

394.sa: एवमाश्वास्य वैदेहीं हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। गमनाय मतिं कृत्वा वैदेहीमभ्यवादयत्।।5.56.8।।
394.e: Hanuman, son of the Windgod having consoled Vaidehi, saluted her respectfully and decided to depart.

394.sa: ततस्स कपिशार्दूलः स्वामिसन्दर्शनोत्सुकः। आरुरोह गिरिश्रेष्ठमरिष्टमरिमर्दनः।।5.56.9।।
394.e: Then Hanuman, the crusher of enemies, a tiger among vanaras anxious to see his lord ascended the mount Arishta.

394.sa: तुङ्गपद्मकजुष्टाभिर्नीलाभिर्वनराजिभिः। सोत्तरीयमिवाम्भोदैः शृंगान्तरविलम्बिभिः।।5.56.10।।
394.e: Mount Arishta was full of blue forestranges with choicest tall padmaka trees. With clouds hanging on the slopes of mountain peaks, it appeared as though the mountain was wrapped in an upper garment.

394.sa: बोध्यमानमिव प्रीत्या दिवाकरकरैश्शुभैः। उन्मिषन्तमिवोद्धूतैर्लोचनैरिव धातुभिः।।5.56.11।।
394.e: As if the mountain was awakened from sleep by the rays of the blessed Sun. With the colour of glowing minerals exuding, it was as if the mountain was looking out with his eyes open. (The minerals underneath the mud appear when wind blows removing the dust covering them. The glowing minerals are fancied to be eyes of the mountain.)

394.sa: तोयौघननिस्स्वनैर्मन्द्रैः प्राधीतमिव पर्वतम्। प्रगीतमिव विस्पष्टैर्नानाप्रस्रवणस्वनैः।।5.56.12।।
394.e: With the loud sounds of masses of gurgling waters, the mountain appeared as though it was standing and reciting (the Vedas) loudly. With murmuring sounds of different waterfalls, it appeared as though the mountain was singing. (The sage differentiates the steadily trickling watersound from the rhythmic musical sounds of waterfalls.)

394.sa: देवदारुभिरत्युच्चैरूर्ध्वबाहुमिव स्थितम्। प्रपातजलनिर्घोषैः प्राक्रुष्टमिव सर्वतः।।5.56.13।।
394.e: With the tall devadaru trees on the mountain, it appeared as if the sages were standing with shoulders lifted up and performing penance. The sounds of waterfalls filled all over with reverberations.

394.sa: वेपमानमिव श्यामैः कम्पमानैश्शरद्वनैः। वेणुभिर्मारुतोद्धूतैः कूजन्तमिव कीचकैः।।5.56.14।।
394.e: The mountain appeared as if trembling with the dark clouds of autumn. The shrill sounds pasing through the hollow bamboos filled with air appeared as if it was producing sweet musical notes.

394.sa: निश्श्वसन्तमिवामर्षाद्घोरैराशीविषोत्तमैः। नीहारकृतगम्भीरैर्ध्यायन्तमिव गह्वरैः।।5.56.15।।
394.e: The mountain was as though hissing like a dreadful, poisonous snake. With the caves standing majestically covered with mist, the mountain appeared as if it was meditating.

394.sa: मेघपादनिभैः पादैः प्रक्रान्तमिव सर्वतः। जृंम्भमाणमिवाऽकाशे शिखरैरभ्रमालिभिः।।5.56.16।।
394.e: With the ranges of foothills appearing like the feet of clouds traversing, with its peaks like garlands of clouds traversing over the mountain, it made one feel it was yawning.

394.sa: कूटैश्च बहुधा कीर्णैश्शोभितं बहुकन्दरैः। सालतालाश्वकर्णैश्च वंशैश्च बहुभिर्वृतम्।।5.56.17।।
394.e: With many kinds of caves and peaks scattered all over, the mountain looked delightful. It was canopied with numerous trees like Sal, palms, Aswakarnas and bamboos.

394.sa: लतावितानैर्विततैः पुष्पवद्भिरलङ्कृतम्। नानामृगगणाकीर्णं धातुनिष्यन्दभूषितम्।।5.56.18।।
394.e: It was spread with creepers filled with beautiful flowers and herds of animals. The colourful minerals flowing down decorated the mountain.

394.sa: बहुप्रस्रवणोपेतं शिलासञ्चयसङ्कटम्। महर्षियक्षगन्धर्वकिन्नरोरगसेवितम्।।5.56.19।।
394.e: There were many streams of water flowing and rocks making it difficult for the streams to flow. The mountain was inhabited by sages, yakshas, gandharvas, kinnaras and nagas, and uragas.

394.sa: लतापादपसङ्घातं सिंहाध्युषितकन्दरम्। व्याघ्रसङ्घसमाकीर्णं स्वादुमूलफलद्रुमम्।।5.56.20।।
394.e: The clusters of creepers, and trees bearing tasty fruits and roots were uprooted. There were caves inhabited by lions. Herds of tigers were scattered all over (by the impetus of Hanuman's pressure on the mountain).

394.sa: तमारुरोह हनुमान् पर्वतं पवनात्मजः। रामदर्शनशीघ्रेण प्रहर्षेणाभिचोदितः।।5.56.21।।
394.e: Anxious to see Rama soon, the son of the Windgod ascended the mountain happily.

394.sa: तेन पादतलाक्रान्ता रम्येषु गिरिसानुषु। सघोषास्समशीर्यन्त शिलाश्चूर्णीकृतास्ततः।।5.56.22।।
394.e: Crushed under Hanuman's feet the rocks making a loud noise on the beautiful mountain ranges rolled down, reduced to powder.

394.sa: स तमारुह्य शैलेन्द्रं व्यवर्धत महाकपिः। दक्षिणादुत्तरं पारं प्रार्थयन् लवणाम्भसः।।5.56.23।।
394.e: On ascending the king of mountains, desiring to reach the northern shore of the saltwater ocean from the Southern shore, he enlarged his body (in preparation to leap).

394.sa: अधिरुह्य ततो वीरः पर्वतं पवनात्मजः। ददर्श सागरं भीमं मीनोरगनिषेवितम्।।5.56.24।।
394.e: Then the heroic son of the Windgod, who had ascended the mountain saw the dreadful ocean inhabited by fishes and snakes.

394.sa: स मारुत इवाऽकाशं मारुतस्यात्मसम्भवः। प्रपेदे हरिशार्दूलो दक्षिणादुत्तरां दिशम्।।5.56.25।।
394.e: Hanuman, the tiger among monkeys leaped into the sky like the Windgod from the south to the north shore.

394.sa: स तदा पीडितस्तेन कपिना पर्वतोत्तमः। ररास सह तैर्भूतैः प्रविशन्वसुधातलम्।।5.56.26।। कम्पमानैश्च शिखरैः पतद्भिरपि च द्रुमैः।
394.e: Pressed under the feet of Hanuman, the great mountain made loud sound sinking into the earth along with all its creatures, with its shaken mountain peaks and uprooted trees dropping down.

394.sa: तस्योरुवेगोन्मथिताः पादपाः पुष्पशालिनः।।5.56.27।। निपेतुर्भूतले रुग्णाश्शक्रायुधहता इव।
394.e: Shaken by the violent force of Hanuman's thighs, the blossoming trees fell on the ground like sickmen hit by Indra's thunderbolt.

394.sa: कन्दरान्तरसंस्थानां पीडितानां महौजसाम्।।5.56.28।। सिंहानां निनदो भीमो नभो भिन्दन् स शुश्रुवे।
394.e: The dreadful roar of strong lions, lying in mountaincaves was heard cracking the sky when they were crushed in the turmoil.

394.sa: त्रस्तव्यावृत्तवसना व्याकुलीकृतभूषणाः।।5.56.29।। विद्याधर्यः समुत्पेतुस्सहसा धरणीधरात्।
394.e: The Vidyadharis with their clothes slipped and ornaments disarrayed in fear, at once flew from the mountain.

394.sa: अतिप्रमाणा बलिनो दीप्तजिह्वा महाविषाः।।5.56.30।। निपीडितशिरोग्रीवा व्यचेष्टन्त महाहयः।
394.e: Highly powerful, huge and poisonous snakes with their glowing tongues protruded, pressed on their heads and necks (by Hanuman).

394.sa: किन्नरोरगन्धर्वयक्षविद्याधरास्तदा।।5.56.31।। पीडितं तं नगवरं त्यक्त्वा गगनमास्थिता:।
394.e: Then the kinnaras, uragas, gandhravas, yakshas and vidyadharas left the tortured mountain and occupied the sky.

394.sa: स च भूमिधरः श्रीमान्बलिना तेन पीडितः।।5.56.32।। सवृक्षशिखरोदग्रः प्रविवेश रसातलम्।
394.e: Crushed by the powerful Hanuman, that prosperous mountain with its trees standing and tall peaks sank into the underworld.

394.sa: दशयोजनविस्तारस्त्रिंशद्योजनमुच्छ्रितः।।5.56.33।। धरण्यां समतां यातः स बभूव धराधरः।
394.e: That mountain of ten yojanas in width and thirty yojanas in height got levelled with the earth.

394.sa: स लिलङ्घयिषुर्भीमं सलीलं लवणार्णवम्।।5.56.34।। कल्लोलास्फालवेलान्तमुत्पपात नभो हरिः।
394.e: Eager to leap the terrific ocean lashed by huge waves hitting the shore Hanuman rose up effortlessly and jumped into the sky. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the  fiftysixth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

395.sa: स चन्द्रकुमुदं रम्यं सार्ककारण्डवं शुभम्। तिष्यश्रवणकादम्बमभ्रशैवालशाद्वलम्।।5.57.1।। पुनर्वसुमहामीनं लोहिताङ्गमहाग्रहम्। ऐरावतमहाद्वीपं स्वातिहंसविलोलितम्।।5.57.2।। वातसङ्घातजातोर्मि चन्द्रांशुशिशिराम्बुमत्। भुजङ्गयक्षगन्धर्वप्रबुद्धकमलोत्पलम्।।5.57.3।। हनुमान्मारुतगतिर्महानौरिव सागरम्। अपारमपरिश्रान्तः पुप्लुवे गगनार्णवम् ।।5.57.4।।
395.e: Hanuman leaped ike the Windgod, unwearied across the sky, as a huge boat crosses an ocean. The ocean was graced with a swan, the sky with constellation of Swati with fullblown lotuses and water lilies, like the nagas, yakshas, and gandharvas gathered together. The Moon in the sky was like a white lotus, the Sun like a waterfowl, the auspicious Tishya and Shravana like the sweetvoiced swans, and the clouds like duckweeds and green grassy spots on the shore. The Punarvasu star was like a large fish and the planet Mars was like a crocodile. Airavata was like the great island. The waves produced by the wind were like cool moonlight in the cold water.

395.sa: स चन्द्रकुमुदं रम्यं सार्ककारण्डवं शुभम्। तिष्यश्रवणकादम्बमभ्रशैवालशाद्वलम्।।5.57.1।। पुनर्वसुमहामीनं लोहिताङ्गमहाग्रहम्। ऐरावतमहाद्वीपं स्वातिहंसविलोलितम्।।5.57.2।। वातसङ्घातजातोर्मि चन्द्रांशुशिशिराम्बुमत्। भुजङ्गयक्षगन्धर्वप्रबुद्धकमलोत्पलम्।।5.57.3।। हनुमान्मारुतगतिर्महानौरिव सागरम्। अपारमपरिश्रान्तः पुप्लुवे गगनार्णवम् ।।5.57.4।।
395.e: Hanuman leaped ike the Windgod, unwearied across the sky, as a huge boat crosses an ocean. The ocean was graced with a swan, the sky with constellation of Swati with fullblown lotuses and water lilies, like the nagas, yakshas, and gandharvas gathered together. The Moon in the sky was like a white lotus, the Sun like a waterfowl, the auspicious Tishya and Shravana like the sweetvoiced swans, and the clouds like duckweeds and green grassy spots on the shore. The Punarvasu star was like a large fish and the planet Mars was like a crocodile. Airavata was like the great island. The waves produced by the wind were like cool moonlight in the cold water.

395.sa: स चन्द्रकुमुदं रम्यं सार्ककारण्डवं शुभम्। तिष्यश्रवणकादम्बमभ्रशैवालशाद्वलम्।।5.57.1।। पुनर्वसुमहामीनं लोहिताङ्गमहाग्रहम्। ऐरावतमहाद्वीपं स्वातिहंसविलोलितम्।।5.57.2।। वातसङ्घातजातोर्मि चन्द्रांशुशिशिराम्बुमत्। भुजङ्गयक्षगन्धर्वप्रबुद्धकमलोत्पलम्।।5.57.3।। हनुमान्मारुतगतिर्महानौरिव सागरम्। अपारमपरिश्रान्तः पुप्लुवे गगनार्णवम् ।।5.57.4।।
